title: Review: Gravitational potential and energy; Power and efficiency; Momentum and its conservation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: E03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; E03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; D09-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; D09-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C04-2#N.6a, D09-1#N.7, E03-1#N.15, C04-2#N.4, D09-1#N.10b, E03-1#N.14, C04-2#N.2, D09-1#N.16b, D09-1#N.2, D09-1#N.5. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Power
items.clue: Rate of doing work, or rate of energy transfer.

items.label: Watt
items.clue: Unit equal to one joule transferred each second.

items.label: Momentum
items.clue: Vector equal to mass × velocity, measured in kg m s⁻¹.

items.label: Newton's third law
items.clue: Reason two colliding bodies push each other with equal and opposite forces.

questions.stem: The escape speed from the surface of planet X is v₀. Planet Y has the same mass as planet X but four times its radius. What is the escape speed from the surface of planet Y?

Two blocks, of masses 1.0 kg and 4.0 kg, are held at rest on a horizontal surface with negligible friction, with a compressed spring between them. When they are released, the 1.0 kg block moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about the 4.0 kg block is correct?

options.text: It moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 0.50 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 8.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It stays at rest, as the total momentum must stay zero.

questions.explanation: Total momentum starts at zero and stays zero: 4.0 × v = 1.0 × 2.0, so v = 0.50 m s⁻¹, opposite to the 1.0 kg block.

questions.stem: Motor A raises a 200 N load through 3.0 m in 6.0 s. Motor B raises a 100 N load through 6.0 m in 4.0 s. Both lift at constant speed. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A develops more power, as it lifts the heavier load.
B does more work, as it lifts its load twice as high.
Both do equal work, and B develops more power.
Both develop equal power, as they do equal work.

questions.explanation: Each does 600 J (200 × 3.0 and 100 × 6.0). B does it in less time: 600 ÷ 4.0 = 150 W against 600 ÷ 6.0 = 100 W.

questions.stem: A probe is launched straight up from the surface of a planet with exactly the escape speed. The planet has no atmosphere, its motion is negligible, and the only force exerted on the probe after launch is the planet's gravitational force. Which statement describes the probe's motion after launch?

options.text: It slows down until it is beyond the reach of gravity, then moves at a constant speed.
It slows to a stop at a large but finite distance, then falls back to the planet.
It slows down all the time, its speed approaching zero as its distance approaches infinity.
It speeds up as it moves away, since U_g decreases as its distance increases.

questions.stem: A 0.50 kg cart moving at 5.0 m/s collides with a 3.0 kg cart at rest on a level track with negligible friction. After the collision, the 0.50 kg cart moves backward at 1.0 m/s and the 3.0 kg cart moves forward at 1.0 m/s. How much of the system's kinetic energy is transformed into other forms of energy?

A cart starts from rest on a level track with negligible friction. A constant horizontal force is exerted on the cart, and no other horizontal force acts on it. At time t after the cart starts, the power delivered to the cart by the force is P. The power delivered by the force at time 2t is how many times P?

A satellite in a circular orbit of radius r around a planet has kinetic energy K₀. The satellite is moved to a circular orbit of radius 4r around the same planet. What is its kinetic energy in the new orbit?

A skater of mass M stands at rest on level ice, where friction is negligible, and throws a ball of mass m horizontally with speed v relative to the ice. Which expression gives the skater's velocity immediately after the throw?

options.text: v, in the direction opposite to the ball
mv/M, in the direction opposite to the ball
Zero, since the skater remains at rest
mv/(M + m), in the direction opposite to the ball

questions.explanation: Total momentum starts at zero, and the throw forces are internal. After the throw, mv + M × (skater's velocity) = 0, so the skater moves back at mv/M, more slowly than the ball because M > m.

questions.stem: A baseball of mass m moving horizontally with speed v is struck by a bat. It leaves the bat moving horizontally with speed 3v/2 in the opposite direction. Taking the ball's initial direction of motion as positive, what is the change in the ball's momentum?

Two carts collide on a level track. Friction and air resistance are negligible. During the collision, Earth exerts a gravitational force and the track exerts a normal force on each cart. Is the total momentum of the two-cart system constant during the collision?

options.text: Yes, because Earth's and the track's forces are internal.
No, because the carts exert large forces on each other.
Yes, because the external forces on the system add up to zero.
No, because each cart's velocity changes in the collision.
